name: Schelling's board: counting 8 or 24 neighbors
description: Schelling's board counting the eight surrounding squares or "the 24 surrounding squares in a 5 × 5 area", equal numbers, half alike wanted. Schelling (p. 164, stated without a figure): enlarging the neighborhood "attenuates the tendency to segregate, at least for moderate demands and near-equal numbers". Measured (release, seeds 1–20, recorded 2026-09-29): mean like share 0.80 with eight neighbors, 0.77 with 24 (counted over each one's own neighborhood).
